# Independent audit: explicit small-endpoint necessity

Source: `candidate 6b20e938071f0379`,
including its additive-reserve Section 4. Result: PASS. One minor proof-order
clarification was requested: infer h>2 from tau>=delta_*>0 BEFORE using the
contraction factor 3/H. A level line has zero planar area, so that inference
is immediate and makes the factor visibly less than one. No new assumption
or mathematical repair is necessary.

## 1. Coupled actual cap inputs

The ordinary cap-cover profiles and the bad nonheavy assumption give
delta=a-u-v>=w/4 and b>=(9/4)q+(5/2-r)w. All A cuts are proper,
so 0<u<=v<=w. The shifted three caps at levels -1,-1,2 cover the
whole plane because their normal sum and threshold sum are both zero.
The profile with minimum cap area min(u,tau) gives
tau>=delta+(3/4)min(u,tau). If tau<u this forces tau>=4delta>=w>=u,
contradiction. Therefore the ACTUAL third-direction tail satisfies
tau>=delta_*=delta+3u/4>0.

It follows that h>2. Contracting the ORIGINAL largest A cap toward an
actual bottom-section point by 3/H stays inside that cap and lies at
levels at most 2. Its area is 9w/H^2 and it is disjoint in area from
the far tail. Hence theta=delta_*/w<=1-9/H^2, proving
H>=3/sqrt(1-theta) and 1/4<=r<theta<1. This retains the relation
theta-r=3u/(4w); the two tail conditions are not optimized independently.

The whole swept segment gives b<=12q/H. Its stronger version
4q>=Hb/3+tau>=Hb/3+theta w was independently audited in
`historical context (not an accepted premise)`, including
the two distinct boundary gains that justify adding tau.

## 2. Preliminary 1/5 elimination

Combining the profile and the segment bound gives
(5/2-r)w<=b[1-9/(16sqrt(1-theta))]. Its positive left side implies
s=sqrt(1-theta)>9/16, while theta>=1/4 gives s<=sqrt(3)/2.
From v<=w and x=u/w=(4/3)(theta-r),
a/w<=1+4theta/3-r/3. At fixed theta its ratio to 5/2-r is
strictly increasing in r, with derivative numerator 1/6+4theta/3.
Replacing r by theta yields exactly the source's g(s).

The identity for 1/5-g(s), its translation z=s-7/8, and the lower
quadratic 177z^2+(23/4)z+55/64 all check exactly. Its discriminant
is -9206/16. Since z>-5/16, the cubic-to-quadratic comparison is
in the correct direction. Thus the preliminary strict 1/5 bound
holds over the complete stated interval.

## 3. Additive reserve and the stronger exact constant

Using q>=Hb/12+theta w/4 in the profile gives exactly

    [5/2-r+(9/16)theta]w <= b[1-9/(16s)].

At fixed theta, the derivative of the corresponding numerator ratio
is positive with numerator 1/6+(55/48)theta. Because u>0, one has
r<theta STRICTLY, so the final a/b<G(s) is strict even if all other
inequalities are equalities. Substituting theta=1-s^2 gives

    G(s)=(2-s^2)(16s-9)/[s(33+7s^2)].

Its derivative is -P(s)/[s^2(7s^2+33)^2] with exactly the displayed
quartic P. The derivative P'=s[252s^2+4512s-1350] is positive
on s>9/16 because its bracket is increasing there and equals
81135/64 at 9/16. The endpoint value
P(sqrt(3)/2)=564sqrt(3)-17037/16 is negative, even after replacing
sqrt(3) by the strictly larger 7/4. Thus P<0 and G is strictly
increasing on the entire relevant interval.

The endpoint evaluation is exactly (80-30sqrt(3))/153, and its
strict comparison with 3/16 reduces to
821^2=674041<691200=3*480^2. Consequently

    a/b < (80-30sqrt(3))/153 < 3/16.

Every eliminated variable came from actual cap or section data;
the result is only a necessary small-A restriction in the specified
bad three-cap branch. It does not claim that the remaining volume
range is impossible or identify a numerical value for an unrelated
compactness threshold.

Independent checker:
`supporting computation verify_explicit_small_endpoint_audit_slab_recovery.py`.

## 4. Added whole-A height restriction and the strict 1/6 split

The subsequent Section 5 is independently PASS. Put alpha=a/w>1.
Lower-cap BM on the SAME A at levels -1,2,h gives the stated
J(alpha,theta), because the lower cap at2 has mass at most a-delta_*.
All square roots and the denominator are positive since theta<1.
The identities

    J_alpha/J=(1/Y-1/X)/(2e),
    J_theta/J=(1+e/Y)/(2(1-theta))

follow by rationalizing the radical differences and are exact. They
give J>=3/sqrt(1-theta), J_theta>=3/2 on theta>=1/4, and
J_theta>=J when alpha>=5/4 and theta>=1/4, since then e/Y>=1/2.

The feasible constraints imply theta>=max(r,3(alpha-1)/4+r/4).
Reducing theta to this value keeps N positive, increases its numerator,
and decreases its denominator. On the two resulting r pieces the
quotient derivatives have precisely the signs of -3J_theta D+7N
and -3J_theta D+55N. The estimates D>=33/16 and the displayed
J bounds make both negative. The formulas match continuously at
the switch, so reducing r to1/4 legitimately increases the bound
over the entire relaxed interval. No unproved maximizer is invoked.

For 1<alpha<=9/8, the first exact bound is (8-3sqrt(3))/17<1/6.
For 9/8<=alpha<=5/4, J(9/8,1/4)=1+sqrt(7) gives the second
bound (65-15sqrt(7))/153<1/6. Both strict radical comparisons
are certified by the stated positive integer squares.

For alpha>=5/4, along theta=3alpha/4-11/16, the derivative
N'<=-9J/64 and D-alpha D'=477/256 give the displayed strictly
negative derivative numerator bound -261/1024. This is used only
where theta<1 and N>0, which every original admissible configuration
requires. If N ceases to be positive, that interval is excluded
instead of being optimized. Thus every actual configuration in the
stated scope has a<b/6.

## 5. Added second residual intersection and the strict 1/9 split

The source now explicitly defines the original mixed set as exactly
the three positive-area fibers A,K,B. This precision is essential
for the identity Q-u=the tested middle-cap area below. The author's
scope clarification has been incorporated.

Section 6 also passes. If a-u-w>0, the two actual open residual
intersections provide P,R strictly missing the u cap, with the v
coordinate spanning a length D>3. Their entire segment strictly
misses that cap. Since B is on its normal's <=1 side, the midpoint
of the segment plus B lies strictly in the MISSED middle halfspace.
An area-preserving shear in the v direction gives exact segment
extrusion b+D W_B> b+3W_B>=2b. The last inequality follows from
B's full longitudinal range being at most3, not from a projection
integral substituted for its actual mass. Therefore

    k-Q+u>b/2.

Combining with the middle profile gives exactly
k>(9/10)b-u+(4/5)v+w/5. Comparing with the bad-target upper bound
k<=a+b-2F gives b/10>(7/10-r)w+(9/5)v. Every denominator in the
subsequent ratios is positive because r<=theta<175/256. Under
y=v/w>1-r, the ratio derivative has numerator 7-28r-18x<=0.
This proves the displayed bound (1+x)/(25-28r).

For theta<=4/7 the exact identity 28r+9x=16r+12theta<=16 gives
the 1/9 bound. For theta>=4/7, monotonicity of the previously
proved G gives a/b<G(sqrt(3/7))<1/9; its endpoint evaluation and
the integer comparison 65712<68607 are correct. This additional
claim remains conditional on the SECOND positive residual overlap;
it is not an unconditional strengthening of the 1/6 theorem.

## 6. Latest Section 7: conditional one-twelfth bound

**PASS.** The audited normal-cone injection adds the actual missed-A
area a-u disjointly from the whole residual segment+B, giving
k-Q+u>b/2+(a-u)/4. Combining with Q>=(4/9)(k+F) gives exactly
k>(9/10)b+(9/20)a-(29/20)u+(4/5)v+w/5. Subtracting this from the
bad upper bound k<=a+b-2F and using a=u+v+rw yields
b>(7-11r/2)w+(45/2)v, with no reversed inequality.

For x=u/w, y=v/w>1-r, the ratio's derivative in y has numerator
7-28r-(45/2)x<=0 because r>=1/4 and x>=0. Its denominator at the lower
endpoint is 59/2-28r>0 in the established range. Therefore the claimed
upper bound (1+x)/(59/2-28r) is valid. Since theta=r+3x/4, the condition
theta<=5/8 gives 28r+12x=12r+16theta<=28theta<=35/2, proving the
strict a/b<1/12 bound there.

For theta>=5/8, s<=sqrt(3/8), which lies above 9/16 and within the
already proved monotonicity interval of G. The evaluation
G(sqrt(3/8))=[208-117/sqrt(3/8)]/285 is exact. Comparing it with 1/12
reduces to sqrt(3/8)<468/737; both sides are positive and the square
certificate is 1,629,507<1,752,192. Hence the second range is covered.
The additional two-residual hypothesis remains explicit; the source
does not promote this conditional result to all configurations.

The updated independent verifier now passes 947 exact checks, including
the new derivative, elimination, and radical comparisons. No correction
identified.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
